This **state-agnostic** notebook asks whether the weather year behind our analysis
is typical, mild, or extreme — and whether that choice would move the findings
we take to PUCs.

Every HP-rate testimony in this repo hangs on the same claim: **new T&D costs
are caused in a small set of peak hours, and those hours are overwhelmingly
summer.** Heat pumps add most of their incremental kWh in winter, when
marginal T&D cost is near zero, so a flat volumetric delivery rate overcharges
them. That claim is a statement about *a year*. A colder winter, or a year
whose system peak flipped into January, would move the May–September share of
peak hours, the incremental peak-hour kWh, the MC heatmaps, and the bills.

We currently run CAIRO on NREL ResStock **AMY 2018** (actual meteorological
year 2018).

> **Demonstration**: the `STATE_PROFILE` below is filled in for Connecticut.
> **This notebook is meant to be copied.** For another state, duplicate the
> file and replace that one profile.

---

## How to use

1. Copy this file. In Parameters, replace `STATE_PROFILE` with the new state's
   system-load URI, GHCN stations, marginal-cost utility, and (for the dollar
   comparison) the CAIRO batch.
2. `YEARS` defaults to **2018–2025**. Edit the list to add or drop years.
   A short system-load file is kept for the temperature charts and dropped
   from the top-N peak split.
3. Optional: `N_PEAK_HOURS` (default 100; MD bulk-tx testimony uses 150).
4. Re-render (`quarto render weather_years.qmd`) or restart the kernel and run
   all cells. GHCN is cached under `cache/`; loads and marginal costs come from S3.

ISO-NE's CT zone file for **2018 starts in July**. Peak-hour shares are only
computed for years with at least 8,700 hours; 2018 still appears in the
temperature charts and in the ResStock overlay.

---

## Why weather year matters

Two clocks run in the CAIRO pipeline and they are easy to mix up:

| Clock | Typical value | What it controls |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **Weather year** | AMY **2018** | EnergyPlus weather that shaped ResStock heating, cooling, and HP COP |
| **Run / calendar year** | **2025** | Weekdays and holidays the 8,760 is rotated onto; MC timestamps; tariff year |
| **MC load year** | often **2025** (sometimes 2018) | Which year's ISO/utility load identifies the top-N peak hours |
| **Price / dollar year** | 2024–2026 | LBMP/ICAP, AESC `$`/kW-yr, CPI, fuel prices |

CAIRO does **not** join marginal cost to building load by calendar date. It
aligns the two 8,760s **by position** after rotating AMY 2018 so Monday maps
to Monday of `year_run`. Changing the weather year without rebuilding ResStock
does nothing. Changing `year_run` without rebuilding month-hour / holiday-aware
MC misaligns day types.

NREL ResStock **2024.2** publishes only **AMY 2018** and **TMY3** (same building
models). **AMY 2012** exists only in the older 2022.1 release. This notebook
therefore compares **observed** weather and **observed** system load across
calendar years, and overlays ResStock's AMY 2018 outdoor temperature on 2018
GHCN. It does not re-run CAIRO.

---

## Data sources

| Series | What it is | Where it comes from |
|--------|------------|---------------------|
| **Weather** | Daily temperature, HDD, CDD | Weighted mean of the GHCN stations in `STATE_PROFILE` (weights are ResStock building counts in the CT example; not NOAA nClimDiv, which is monthly) |
| **System load** | Hourly MW for the whole zone or utility, not ResStock homes | The `load_uri` you paste. See the comment on that field: rate-design-platform does not use one hive shape for every state |
| **ResStock weather check** | EnergyPlus outdoor dry-bulb | A sample of upgrade-00 hourly files. Each building has its own EPW (`in.weather_file_city`); there is no single ResStock station |
| **Representative load** | Weighted-average hourly kWh of fossil-heated homes, pre-HP and post-HP | Same construction as `representative_home.qmd`: master bills for weights, `billing_kwh_8760` for the shape |
| **Marginal cost** | Filed dist and bulk-tx `$`/kWh, plus a top-N reallocation of those annual scalars onto each system-load year | `s3://data.sb/switchbox/marginal_costs/…` usually has one run year. Year-to-year dollar differences below are that scalar moved onto each year's peak hours |

---

## Notebook sections

| Section | What it covers |
|---------|----------------|
| **1 — Outdoor temperature** | GHCN daily mean, HDD/CDD; how extreme 2018's winter and summer were |
| **2 — System electricity** | Zone/utility 8760, monthly energy, annual peak; incomplete years flagged |
| **3 — Top-N peak hours** | Share in May–Sep vs Oct–Apr (the testimony split) |
| **4 — 2018 among its neighbors** | Rank 2018 on HDD, CDD, summer-peak share, winter/summer peak ratio |
| **5 — ResStock vs GHCN 2018** | Sample of AMY 2018 outdoor temp against the airport series |
| **6 — Load-weighted PoP and a KDE year** | Top-100 load-weighted weights by year, for the dist series and the bulk-tx series, then one analysis-year 8760 from a KDE trained on those years |
| **7 — Marginal cost on a representative load** | Filed schedule, then the same home and the same `$`/kW-yr allocated with each year's load-weighted top 100, including the heat-pump increment |

```{python}
def year_color_scale(years: list[int]):
    return scale_color_manual(
        values={str(y): YEAR_COLORS.get(y, "#888888") for y in years}
    )


def year_fill_scale(years: list[int]):
    return scale_fill_manual(
        values={str(y): YEAR_COLORS.get(y, "#888888") for y in years}
    )


def quiet(fn, *args, **kwargs):
    """Run `fn` with stdout discarded. RDP loaders print DST housekeeping."""
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        return fn(*args, **kwargs)


def show_gt(
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    title: str,
    subtitle: str | None = None,
    *,
    labels: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    int_cols: Sequence[str] = (),
    num_cols: Sequence[str] = (),
    num_decimals: int = 1,
) -> None:
    table = GT(df.to_pandas())
    table = (
        table.tab_header(title=title, subtitle=subtitle)
        if subtitle
        else table.tab_header(title=title)
    )
    if labels:
        table = table.cols_label(**labels)
    if int_cols:
        table = table.fmt_integer(columns=list(int_cols))
    if num_cols:
        table = table.fmt_number(columns=list(num_cols), decimals=num_decimals)
    display_gt(table.tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options()))
```

## Section 1: Outdoor temperature

Daily max and min from NOAA GHCN at every station in `ghcn_stations`. Mean
daily temperature at a station is `(TMAX + TMIN) / 2` when TAVG is blank.
The **statewide** series is the weighted mean of those stations on each
day. The weight is the third field on each station (ResStock building count
in the demonstration). HDD and CDD use a 65 °F base on that mean.

This is not NOAA nClimDiv (that product is monthly and area-weighted) and it
is not the EPW ResStock simulated. Section 5 checks whether AMY 2018's
building dry-bulb tracks this statewide mean.

```{python}
#| label: load-ghcn

def fetch_ghcn(station: str, years: list[int]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    start, end = min(years), max(years)
    cache_path = CACHE_DIR / f"ghcn_{station}_{start}_{end}.parquet"
    if cache_path.exists():
        return pl.read_parquet(cache_path)
    url = (
        "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1"
        f"?dataset=daily-summaries&stations={station}"
        f"&startDate={start}-01-01&endDate={end}-12-31"
        "&dataTypes=TMAX,TMIN,TAVG&units=standard&format=csv"
    )
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        headers={"User-Agent": "Switchbox weather-years notebook (https://switch.box/)"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        csv_bytes = resp.read()
    raw = pl.read_csv(csv_bytes, infer_schema_length=0)
    # NCEI sends TMAX/TMIN as strings; units=standard is Fahrenheit.
    parsed = (
        raw.rename({c: c.lower() for c in raw.columns})
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("date").str.to_date(),
            pl.col("tmax").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False),
            pl.col("tmin").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False),
            (
                pl.col("tavg").cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
                if "tavg" in [c.lower() for c in raw.columns]
                else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Float64)
            ).alias("tavg_reported"),
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.coalesce(
                pl.col("tavg_reported"),
                (pl.col("tmax") + pl.col("tmin")) / 2,
            ).alias("tavg_f")
        )
        .select("date", "tmax", "tmin", "tavg_f")
        .drop_nulls("tavg_f")
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("date").dt.year().alias("year"),
            pl.col("date").dt.month().alias("month"),
            pl.col("date").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
            (HDD_BASE_F - pl.col("tavg_f")).clip(lower_bound=0).alias("hdd"),
            (pl.col("tavg_f") - HDD_BASE_F).clip(lower_bound=0).alias("cdd"),
        )
    )
    parsed.write_parquet(cache_path)
    return parsed


station_frames = []
for row in profile["ghcn_stations"]:
    station_id, station_name = row[0], row[1]
    weight = float(row[2]) if len(row) > 2 else 1.0
    one = fetch_ghcn(station_id, YEARS).with_columns(
        pl.lit(station_id).alias("station_id"),
        pl.lit(station_name).alias("station"),
        pl.lit(weight).alias("weight"),
    )
    station_frames.append(one)
stations = pl.concat(station_frames, how="vertical_relaxed").filter(pl.col("year").is_in(YEARS))
wx = (
    stations.group_by("date")
    .agg(
        ((pl.col("tmax") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum()).alias("tmax"),
        ((pl.col("tmin") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum()).alias("tmin"),
        ((pl.col("tavg_f") * pl.col("weight")).sum() / pl.col("weight").sum()).alias("tavg_f"),
        pl.len().alias("n_stations"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("date").dt.year().alias("year"),
        pl.col("date").dt.month().alias("month"),
        pl.col("date").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
        (HDD_BASE_F - pl.col("tavg_f")).clip(lower_bound=0).alias("hdd"),
        (pl.col("tavg_f") - HDD_BASE_F).clip(lower_bound=0).alias("cdd"),
    )
    .sort("date")
)
show_gt(
    wx.group_by("year")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("Days"),
        pl.col("n_stations").mean().round(1).alias("Stations"),
    )
    .sort("year")
    .rename({"year": "Year"}),
    title="Days in the statewide mean",
    subtitle="A station with a missing day drops out of that day's mean only.",
    int_cols=["Days"],
    num_cols=["Stations"],
    num_decimals=1,
)
display_gt(
    GT(
        stations.group_by("station", "weight")
        .agg(
            pl.len().alias("Days"),
            pl.col("tavg_f").mean().round(1).alias("mean_f"),
        )
        .sort("weight", descending=True)
        .to_pandas()
    )
    .tab_header(
        title="GHCN stations in the statewide mean",
        subtitle="Weights are ResStock building counts. A station with a missing day drops out of that day only.",
    )
    .cols_label(station="Station", weight="Buildings", mean_f="Mean °F")
    .fmt_integer(columns=["weight", "Days"])
    .fmt_number(columns=["mean_f"], decimals=1)
    .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
)
```

A year with more HDD than 2018 is a *colder* heating season: ResStock AMY 2018
would understate HP heating kWh relative to that year. More CDD means a
hotter cooling season, which moves *both* the pre-HP air-conditioning load and
the system summer peak.

### How extreme was 2018?

ResStock's weather file is one calendar year. The question for rate design is
whether that year's **winter** and **summer** were typical of the window we
compare against. A colder October–April means more heat-pump kWh than AMY 2018
shows. A hotter May–September means more pre-HP cooling load and a higher
system peak than AMY 2018 shows.

Heating and cooling seasons here are October–April and May–September of the
*same* calendar year — the same 12-month window as the AMY file, not a winter
that straddles two years.

```{python}
#| label: 2018-extremes

season_wx = (
    wx.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in(list(HEATING_MONTHS)))
        .then(pl.col("hdd"))
        .otherwise(0.0)
        .alias("hdd_heat"),
        pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))
        .then(pl.col("cdd"))
        .otherwise(0.0)
        .alias("cdd_cool"),
    )
    .group_by("year")
    .agg(
        pl.col("hdd_heat").sum().round(0).cast(pl.Int64).alias("heating_hdd"),
        pl.col("cdd_cool").sum().round(0).cast(pl.Int64).alias("cooling_cdd"),
        pl.col("tavg_f")
        .filter(pl.col("month").is_in(list(HEATING_MONTHS)))
        .mean()
        .alias("heat_mean_f"),
        pl.col("tavg_f")
        .filter(pl.col("month").is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))
        .mean()
        .alias("cool_mean_f"),
    )
    .sort("year")
)
y0 = RESSTOCK_WEATHER_YEAR
row = season_wx.filter(pl.col("year") == y0)
others = season_wx.filter(pl.col("year") != y0)


def _rank_high(frame: pl.DataFrame, col: str, year: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    ordered = frame.sort(col, descending=True)
    place = ordered["year"].to_list().index(year) + 1
    return place, ordered.height


hdd_place, hdd_n = _rank_high(season_wx, "heating_hdd", y0)
cdd_place, cdd_n = _rank_high(season_wx, "cooling_cdd", y0)
heat_2018 = float(row["heat_mean_f"][0])
cool_2018 = float(row["cool_mean_f"][0])
heat_other = float(others["heat_mean_f"].mean())
cool_other = float(others["cool_mean_f"].mean())
winter_delta = heat_2018 - heat_other
summer_delta = cool_2018 - cool_other
winter_phrase = (
    f"{abs(winter_delta):.1f} °F colder than the mean of the other years"
    if winter_delta < 0
    else f"{abs(winter_delta):.1f} °F warmer than the mean of the other years"
)
summer_phrase = (
    f"{abs(summer_delta):.1f} °F hotter than the mean of the other years"
    if summer_delta > 0
    else f"{abs(summer_delta):.1f} °F cooler than the mean of the other years"
)
both_severe = winter_delta < 0 and summer_delta > 0
tail = (
    "Both tails were on the severe side of this window: a colder winter raises "
    "heat-pump kWh relative to a typical year, and a hotter summer raises "
    "pre-HP cooling load and the system peak."
    if both_severe
    else "The monthly anomaly chart shows which months drove that."
)
display(
    Markdown(
        f"**{y0} heating season** (Oct–Apr) was {winter_phrase} "
        f"({hdd_place} of {hdd_n} for HDD). "
        f"**{y0} cooling season** (May–Sep) was {summer_phrase} "
        f"({cdd_place} of {cdd_n} for CDD). {tail}"
    )
)
```

Negative bars in the chart below are months that were **colder** than the mean
of the other years; positive bars are **warmer**. Look at October–April for
the heating-season story and May–September for the cooling-season story.

## Section 2: System electricity

These are the zonal (or utility) 8,760s the marginal-cost pipelines rank to
place `$`/kW-yr onto peak hours. For CT that is ISO-NE's CT zone; for MD, BGE's
PJM-zone utility load; for RI, the ISO-NE RI zone. We are not using ResStock
here — we want the *system's* weather-driven peak calendar, which is what
testimony means by "peak hours."

Monthly energy (GWh) and the annual peak MW include everything on the zone —
C&I, EVs, losses — not just ResStock residential. That is the right series
for "when is the system constrained?"

A year with fewer than 8,700 hours is dropped from the peak-hour tables so a
missing January cannot masquerade as a winter-peaking system. It still appears
in the temperature charts above. Coverage is in the annual table.

```{python}
#| label: load-iso

def load_iso_year(year: int) -> pl.DataFrame | None:
    uri = profile["load_uri"].format(year=year)
    ts_col = profile["ts_col"]
    load_col = profile["load_col"]
    try:
        raw = cast(
            pl.DataFrame,
            pl.scan_parquet(uri, storage_options=S3_OPTS, hive_partitioning=True).collect(),
        )
    except Exception:
        return None
    if ts_col not in raw.columns or load_col not in raw.columns:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{year}: missing {ts_col!r} or {load_col!r}; columns={raw.columns}"
        )
    return (
        raw.select(
            pl.col(ts_col).alias("timestamp"),
            pl.col(load_col).cast(pl.Float64).alias("load_mw"),
        )
        .drop_nulls()
        .unique(subset=["timestamp"])
        .sort("timestamp")
        .with_columns(
            pl.lit(year).alias("year"),
            pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month"),
            pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
            pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
        )
    )


iso_years: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
for year in YEARS:
    frame = load_iso_year(year)
    if frame is not None:
        iso_years.append(frame)

if not iso_years:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"No system-load years loaded for {STATE}. Check load_uri in STATE_PROFILE."
    )

iso = pl.concat(iso_years, how="vertical_relaxed")
iso_complete_years = sorted(
    iso.group_by("year")
    .len()
    .filter(pl.col("len") >= MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE)["year"]
    .to_list()
)
```

## Section 3: Top-N peak hours, summer vs winter

For each complete year, take the `N_PEAK_HOURS` hours of highest load — the
same "top 100" rule the dist PoP allocator uses (MD bulk tx uses 150; change
`N_PEAK_HOURS`). Then split those hours into May–September vs October–April.

If May–September's share is stable across years, the testimony's summer-peak
claim is not an artifact of 2018 or of a single recent year. If a cold year
drops that share a lot, the claim needs a caveat.

```{python}
#| label: peak-hours

def peak_table(loads: pl.DataFrame, n_hours: int) -> pl.DataFrame:
    rows = []
    for year, part in loads.group_by("year"):
        y = int(year[0]) if isinstance(year, tuple) else int(year)
        if part.height < MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE:
            continue
        top = part.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(n_hours).with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col("month").is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))
            .then(pl.lit("May–Sep"))
            .when(pl.col("month").is_in(list(HEATING_MONTHS)))
            .then(pl.lit("Oct–Apr"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit("other"))
            .alias("season")
        )
        n = top.height
        n_summer = top.filter(pl.col("season") == "May–Sep").height
        n_heating = top.filter(pl.col("season") == "Oct–Apr").height
        summer_peak = part.filter(pl.col("month").is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))["load_mw"].max()
        winter_peak = part.filter(pl.col("month").is_in([12, 1, 2]))["load_mw"].max()
        rows.append(
            {
                "year": y,
                "n_peak_hours": n,
                "n_may_sep": n_summer,
                "pct_may_sep": round(100 * n_summer / n, 1),
                "n_oct_apr": n_heating,
                "pct_oct_apr": round(100 * n_heating / n, 1),
                "summer_peak_mw": round(float(summer_peak), 0),
                "winter_peak_mw": round(float(winter_peak), 0),
                "winter_over_summer": round(float(winter_peak) / float(summer_peak), 2)
                if summer_peak
                else None,
            }
        )
    return pl.DataFrame(rows).sort("year")


peaks = peak_table(iso, N_PEAK_HOURS)
show_gt(
    peaks,
    title=f"Top {N_PEAK_HOURS} hours by season, {profile['load_label']}",
    subtitle="May–Sep is the testimony summer window. Winter peak is the highest December–February MW; summer peak is the highest May–September MW.",
    labels={
        "year": "Year",
        "n_peak_hours": "Top hours",
        "n_may_sep": "Hours in May–Sep",
        "pct_may_sep": "Share in May–Sep (%)",
        "n_oct_apr": "Hours in Oct–Apr",
        "pct_oct_apr": "Share in Oct–Apr (%)",
        "summer_peak_mw": "May–Sep peak (MW)",
        "winter_peak_mw": "Dec–Feb peak (MW)",
        "winter_over_summer": "Winter/summer peak ratio",
    },
    int_cols=["n_peak_hours", "n_may_sep", "n_oct_apr", "summer_peak_mw", "winter_peak_mw"],
    num_cols=["pct_may_sep", "pct_oct_apr"],
    num_decimals=1,
)
```

The winter/summer peak *ratio* is the system-level analogue of RI's "winter"

## Section 4: Where 2018 sits

Join degree-days to the peak-hour table and rank 2018 among complete load
years. Temperature ranks still include 2018 even when ISO load is incomplete.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-2018-rank
#| tbl-cap: "Where 2018 ranks on weather and on the system peak calendar."

wx_annual = deg_days.select("year", "hdd65", "cdd65", "mean_f")
cmp = wx_annual.join(peaks, on="year", how="left").sort("year")
y0 = RESSTOCK_WEATHER_YEAR
incomplete_note = "Not ranked — ISO load is incomplete"


def _ordinal(n: int) -> str:
    if 10 <= n % 100 <= 20:
        tail = "th"
    else:
        tail = {1: "st", 2: "nd", 3: "rd"}.get(n % 10, "th")
    return f"{n}{tail}"


def standing(
    frame: pl.DataFrame,
    col: str,
    year: int,
    *,
    high_adj: str,
    value_fmt: str,
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    row = frame.filter(pl.col("year") == year)
    if row.height == 0 or row[col].null_count() == row.height:
        return "—", incomplete_note
    ordered = frame.drop_nulls(col).sort(col, descending=True)
    place = ordered["year"].to_list().index(year) + 1
    n = ordered.height
    value = float(row[col][0])
    return value_fmt.format(value), f"{_ordinal(place)}-{high_adj} of {n} years"


hdd_val, hdd_stand = standing(cmp, "hdd65", y0, high_adj="coldest", value_fmt="{:,.0f}")
cdd_val, cdd_stand = standing(cmp, "cdd65", y0, high_adj="hottest", value_fmt="{:,.0f}")
share_val, share_stand = standing(
    cmp, "pct_may_sep", y0, high_adj="most summer-peaking", value_fmt="{:.1f}%"
)
ratio_val, ratio_stand = standing(
    cmp, "winter_over_summer", y0, high_adj="highest winter/summer ratio", value_fmt="{:.2f}"
)
show_gt(
    pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "Metric": [
                "Annual heating degree-days",
                "Annual cooling degree-days",
                "Share of top hours in May–Sep",
                "Winter/summer peak ratio",
            ],
            "2018": [hdd_val, cdd_val, share_val, ratio_val],
            "Standing": [hdd_stand, cdd_stand, share_stand, ratio_stand],
        }
    ),
    title=f"Where {y0} sits among {min(YEARS)}–{max(YEARS)}",
    subtitle="Degree-days include 2018 even when ISO load is incomplete. Peak-hour ranks do not.",
)
show_gt(
    cmp.select(
        "year",
        "hdd65",
        "cdd65",
        "mean_f",
        "pct_may_sep",
        "winter_over_summer",
    ),
    title=f"{y0} versus every requested year",
    labels={
        "year": "Year",
        "hdd65": "HDD",
        "cdd65": "CDD",
        "mean_f": "Mean °F",
        "pct_may_sep": "May–Sep share of top hours (%)",
        "winter_over_summer": "Winter/summer peak ratio",
    },
    int_cols=["hdd65", "cdd65"],
    num_cols=["mean_f", "pct_may_sep"],
    num_decimals=1,
)
```

Read the ranks before drawing a conclusion. A *mild* 2018 (low HDD, high
May–Sep peak share) would mean our HP bill *increases* are conservative
relative to a colder year, and our "peaks stay in summer" claim is *easier*
in 2018 than in a winter-peaking year. A *harsh* 2018 would be the opposite.

## Section 5: ResStock AMY 2018 vs the statewide mean

ResStock does not use one weather station. Each building is assigned an EPW
file, stored as `in.weather_file_city` on the metadata. The hourly file writes
that file's outdoor dry-bulb as `out.outdoor_air_dryblub_temp.c` (NREL's
spelling). CAIRO never reads the column.

The overlay is the median daily mean across a stride sample of upgrade-00
files, compared with the statewide GHCN mean from Section 1 — not with
Hartford, Bridgeport, or any other single airport. The table under the chart
lists which EPW cities the whole state uses, when local metadata is present.

```{python}
#| label: fig-resstock-vs-ghcn
#| fig-cap: "Daily mean outdoor temperature in 2018: statewide GHCN mean vs median of a ResStock AMY 2018 sample."

def sample_resstock_daily_temp(
    hourly_dir: Path, n: int
) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame | None, int, int]:
    if not hourly_dir.is_dir():
        return None, 0, 0
    files = sorted(hourly_dir.glob("*.parquet"))
    if not files:
        return None, 0, 0
    stride = max(1, len(files) // n)
    picked = files[::stride][:n]
    daily_parts = []
    for path in picked:
        raw = pl.scan_parquet(str(path))
        names = raw.collect_schema().names()
        if OUTDOOR_TEMP_C not in names or "timestamp" not in names:
            continue
        daily_parts.append(
            raw.select("timestamp", pl.col(OUTDOOR_TEMP_C).alias("temp_c"))
            .drop_nulls()
            .with_columns(pl.col("timestamp").dt.date().alias("date"))
            .group_by("date")
            .agg(pl.col("temp_c").mean())
            .collect()
        )
    if not daily_parts:
        return None, len(picked), len(files)
    daily = (
        pl.concat(daily_parts)
        .group_by("date")
        .agg(pl.col("temp_c").median().alias("temp_c"))
        .with_columns((pl.col("temp_c") * 9 / 5 + 32).alias("tavg_f"))
        .sort("date")
    )
    return daily, len(picked), len(files)


rs_daily, n_rs_sample, n_rs_files = sample_resstock_daily_temp(
    RESSTOCK_HOURLY_DIR, N_RESSTOCK_SAMPLE
)
if rs_daily is not None:
    ghcn_2018 = wx.filter(pl.col("year") == RESSTOCK_WEATHER_YEAR).select(
        "date", pl.col("tavg_f").alias("ghcn_f")
    )
    overlay = (
        ghcn_2018.join(rs_daily.select("date", pl.col("tavg_f").alias("resstock_f")), on="date", how="inner")
        .with_columns(pl.col("date").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"))
        .unpivot(
            index=["date", "day_of_year"],
            on=["ghcn_f", "resstock_f"],
            variable_name="series",
            value_name="tavg_f",
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("series").replace_strict(
                {"ghcn_f": WEATHER_LABEL, "resstock_f": "ResStock AMY 2018 (sample median)"}
            )
        )
    )
    p = (
        ggplot(overlay, aes("day_of_year", "tavg_f", color="series"))
        + geom_line(alpha=0.9, size=0.6)
        + scale_color_manual(values={WEATHER_LABEL: SB_COLORS["midnight"], "ResStock AMY 2018 (sample median)": SB_COLORS["carrot"]})
        + labs(
            title="2018 outdoor temperature: GHCN vs ResStock AMY",
            x="",
            y="°F",
            color="",
        )
        + scale_x_continuous(
            breaks=[1, 91, 182, 274, 365],
            labels=["Jan", "Apr", "Jul", "Oct", "Dec"],
        )
        + theme_switchbox()
        + theme(figure_size=(10.5, 4.5))
    )
    display_figure(p.draw())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-resstock-mean

if rs_daily is not None:
    means = (
        overlay.group_by("series")
        .agg(pl.col("tavg_f").mean().round(1).alias("mean_f"))
        .sort("series")
    )
    ghcn_mean = float(means.filter(pl.col("series") == WEATHER_LABEL)["mean_f"][0])
    rs_mean = float(
        means.filter(pl.col("series") == "ResStock AMY 2018 (sample median)")["mean_f"][0]
    )
    display(
        Markdown(
            f"The overlay is the median daily temperature of **{n_rs_sample}** "
            f"buildings sampled from **{n_rs_files:,}** upgrade-00 hourly files. "
            f"The ResStock sample averages **{rs_mean - ghcn_mean:+.1f} °F** "
            f"versus the statewide GHCN mean."
        )
    )
    show_gt(
        means,
        title="2018 mean outdoor temperature",
        labels={"series": "Series", "mean_f": "Mean °F"},
        num_cols=["mean_f"],
        num_decimals=1,
    )
elif n_rs_files == 0:
    display(Markdown("Skipping the ResStock overlay: hourly files are not on this machine."))
else:
    display(Markdown("Skipping the ResStock overlay: none of the sampled files had outdoor dry-bulb."))
```

## Section 6: Load-weighted peak hours, and one KDE year

**Load-weighted top 100, one map per year.** This is how distribution PoP
works in rate-design-platform (`calculate_pop_weights`): take the top
`N_PEAK_HOURS` hours of that year and give each a weight `MW / sum(MW of
those hours)`. The weights sum to 1. An equal split would give every peak
hour `1/100`. The earlier top-N chart only said whether an hour was in the
set. These maps say how much of the annual `$`/kW-yr that hour would carry.

Distribution uses `load_uri`. Bulk transmission uses `bulk_zones` (summed)
or `bulk_load_uri` when that list is empty. For this Connecticut file,
distribution is the CT zone and bulk transmission is the New England system,
which is the series CT's bulk-tx KDE is fit on. They are not the same 8760.

**One analysis-year 8760 from a KDE.** This is CT's bulk-tx default
(`probability_of_peak` in rate-design-platform): normalize each training year
by its own average load, fit a truncated Gaussian KDE in each month ×
weekday-or-weekend × hour cell, and turn the tail above the delimiter into a
probability. That probability is laid onto `analysis_year`'s weekdays and
holidays as `$`/kWh, using the filed schedule's annual `$`/kW-yr so a flat
1 kW load pays that scalar back. The same fit is run twice: once on the
distribution load series, once on bulk transmission. It is not a claim that
the state's filed distribution method is a KDE. It is that method, applied
to the history in `kde_years`.

The KDE puts a **trace** of probability on January and February, so those
tiles appear on the heatmap. They carry almost none of the annual dollars.
CT testimony drops hours under 0.5¢/kWh; after that cut, 100% of peak hours
are May–September. Titles report the **dollar share**, not the hour count.

```{python}
#| label: load-weighted-pop

def naive_wall(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Hour-beginning Eastern wall time, timezone-naive, for the KDE."""
    tz = getattr(df.schema["timestamp"], "time_zone", None)
    if tz is None:
        expr = pl.col("timestamp")
    elif tz == "America/New_York":
        expr = pl.col("timestamp").dt.replace_time_zone(None)
    else:
        expr = (
            pl.col("timestamp")
            .dt.convert_time_zone("America/New_York")
            .dt.replace_time_zone(None)
        )
    return (
        df.with_columns(expr.alias("timestamp"))
        .group_by("timestamp")
        .agg(pl.col("load_mw").mean())
        .sort("timestamp")
    )


def load_weighted_top(df: pl.DataFrame, n: int, year: int) -> pl.DataFrame:
    top = df.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(n)
    total = float(top["load_mw"].sum())
    return top.with_columns(
        (pl.col("load_mw") / total).alias("pop_weight"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
        pl.lit(str(year)).alias("year"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month"),
    )


def plot_weighted_pop(weights: pl.DataFrame, title: str):
    p = (
        ggplot(weights, aes("day_of_year", "hour", fill="pop_weight"))
        + geom_tile()
        + facet_wrap("year", ncol=4)
        + scale_fill_gradient(low="#f8e3c4", high=SB_COLORS["carrot"])
        + scale_x_continuous(
            breaks=[1, 91, 182, 274, 365],
            labels=["Jan", "Apr", "Jul", "Oct", "Dec"],
        )
        + scale_y_continuous(breaks=[0, 6, 12, 18, 23])
        + labs(title=title, x="", y="Hour", fill="Weight")
        + theme_switchbox()
        + theme(figure_size=(10.5, 6.5))
    )
    display_figure(p.draw())


def load_bulk_year(year: int) -> pl.DataFrame | None:
    zones = list(profile.get("bulk_zones") or [])
    if zones:
        rdp = str(profile["rdp_root"])
        if rdp not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, rdp)
        from utils.data_prep.marginal_costs.supply.supply_capacity_isone import (
            load_isone_zone_loads,
        )

        return quiet(
            load_isone_zone_loads,
            str(profile["bulk_zone_s3_base"]),
            zones,
            year,
            S3_OPTS,
        )
    uri = str(profile.get("bulk_load_uri") or "")
    if not uri:
        return None
    raw = cast(
        pl.DataFrame,
        pl.scan_parquet(
            uri.format(year=year),
            storage_options=S3_OPTS,
            hive_partitioning=True,
        ).collect(),
    )
    ts, load = str(profile["bulk_ts_col"]), str(profile["bulk_load_col"])
    return naive_wall(
        raw.select(
            pl.col(ts).alias("timestamp"),
            pl.col(load).cast(pl.Float64).alias("load_mw"),
        )
    )


kde_years = [int(y) for y in profile["kde_years"]]
dist_pop_parts: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
for year in kde_years:
    part = iso.filter(pl.col("year") == year)
    if part.height < MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE:
        continue
    dist_pop_parts.append(load_weighted_top(naive_wall(part), N_PEAK_HOURS, year))

dist_pop = pl.concat(dist_pop_parts) if dist_pop_parts else None
if dist_pop is not None:
    plot_weighted_pop(
        dist_pop,
        f"Load-weighted top {N_PEAK_HOURS}, {profile['load_label']}",
    )

bulk_by_year: dict[int, pl.DataFrame] = {}
bulk_pop_parts: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
n_bulk = int(profile.get("bulk_n_peak_hours") or N_PEAK_HOURS)
for year in kde_years:
    try:
        bulk_year = load_bulk_year(year)
    except Exception as exc:
        continue
    if bulk_year is None or bulk_year.height < MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE:
        continue
    bulk_by_year[year] = bulk_year
    bulk_pop_parts.append(load_weighted_top(bulk_year, n_bulk, year))

bulk_pop = pl.concat(bulk_pop_parts) if bulk_pop_parts else None
if bulk_pop is not None:
    plot_weighted_pop(
        bulk_pop,
        f"Load-weighted top {n_bulk}, {profile['bulk_load_label']}",
    )


def season_share(weights: pl.DataFrame, series: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return (
        weights.group_by("year")
        .agg(
            pl.col("pop_weight")
            .filter(pl.col("month").is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))
            .sum()
            .alias("may_sep")
        )
        .with_columns(pl.lit(series).alias("series"))
        .sort("year")
    )


share_parts = []
if dist_pop is not None:
    share_parts.append(season_share(dist_pop, profile["load_label"]))
if bulk_pop is not None:
    share_parts.append(season_share(bulk_pop, str(profile["bulk_load_label"])))
if share_parts:
    show_gt(
        pl.concat(share_parts)
        .select("series", "year", "may_sep")
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("year").cast(pl.Int64),
            (pl.col("may_sep") * 100).round(1).alias("may_sep_pct"),
        )
        .drop("may_sep"),
        title="Share of load-weighted top-N weight in May–September",
        subtitle="The rest of the weight is October–April. Weights sum to 1 within each year.",
        labels={
            "series": "Load series",
            "year": "Year",
            "may_sep_pct": "May–Sep share (%)",
        },
        num_cols=["may_sep_pct"],
        num_decimals=1,
    )
```

```{python}
#| label: kde-helpers

rdp = str(profile["rdp_root"])
if rdp not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, rdp)
from utils.data_prep.marginal_costs.probability_of_peak import (
    allocate_annual_cost_by_pop,
    probability_of_peak,
)

analysis_year = int(profile["analysis_year"])
scalars = {"Distribution": 1.0, "Transmission": 1.0}
try:
    mc_for_scalar = load_delivery_mc_heatmap(
        STATE, str(profile["mc_utility"]), analysis_year
    )
    scalars["Distribution"] = float(mc_for_scalar["mc_dist_sub_tx"].sum())
    scalars["Transmission"] = float(mc_for_scalar["mc_bulk_tx"].sum())
except Exception:
    mc_for_scalar = None


def _month_expr(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.Expr:
    return pl.col("month") if "month" in df.columns else pl.col("timestamp").dt.month()


def mc_season_stats(df: pl.DataFrame, col: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Dollar share vs hour count in May–Sep. Dollar share is what the titles use."""
    month = _month_expr(df)
    total = float(df[col].sum())
    summer_dollars = float(df.filter(month.is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))[col].sum())
    nz = df.filter(pl.col(col) > 0)
    n_nz = nz.height
    n_summer = nz.filter(_month_expr(nz).is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS))).height
    peak = df.filter(pl.col(col) > MC_PEAK_THRESHOLD)
    n_peak = peak.height
    n_peak_summer = peak.filter(_month_expr(peak).is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS))).height
    return {
        "dollar_share": (summer_dollars / total) if total else 0.0,
        "hour_share": (n_summer / n_nz) if n_nz else 0.0,
        "peak_hour_share": (n_peak_summer / n_peak) if n_peak else 0.0,
        "annual": total,
    }


def mc_heatmap_title(component: str, extra: str, stats: dict[str, float]) -> str:
    dollar = float(stats["dollar_share"])
    hour = float(stats["hour_share"])
    base = f"{component} · {extra} · {dollar:.2%} of annual $ in May–Sep"
    if abs(dollar - hour) >= 0.02:
        return f"{base} ({hour:.0%} of hours with any MC)"
    return base


def kde_8760(history: pl.DataFrame, scalar: float, component: str, load_label: str) -> None:
    years_used = sorted(history["timestamp"].dt.year().unique().to_list())
    pop = probability_of_peak(naive_wall(history))
    hourly = allocate_annual_cost_by_pop(
        pop.cells, scalar, analysis_year, value_col="mc_per_kwh"
    ).with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month"),
    )
    stats = mc_season_stats(hourly, "mc_per_kwh")
    year_lo, year_hi = min(years_used), max(years_used)
    display_figure(
        plot_mc_heatmap(
            hourly,
            "mc_per_kwh",
            title=mc_heatmap_title(
                component,
                f"KDE on {load_label}, {year_lo}–{year_hi}",
                stats,
            ),
            high_color=SB_COLORS["carrot"],
        )
    )


dist_frames = []
for year in kde_years:
    part = iso.filter(pl.col("year") == year)
    if part.height < MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE:
        continue
    dist_frames.append(naive_wall(part))
```

## Section 7: Marginal cost by year, on a representative load

The **filed schedule** is the hourly `$`/kWh parquet CAIRO billed
(`year=2025` on S3). It is a calendar, not a weather year. Connecticut
currently has only that one file.

Two units:

- **System `$`/kW-year** — what a flat 1 kW load would pay. For CT that is
  `$21.22`/kW-yr of distribution (OCC-863, loss-adjusted) and `$72.87`/kW-yr
  of bulk transmission (AESC `$69` in 2024 dollars, CPI to 2026).
- **Household `$`/year** — that schedule times the representative home's
  hourly kWh.

Then three separate questions, each with its own table or chart:

1. **What did CAIRO bill this pre-HP home?** The filed 8760 — OCC-863 for
   distribution, a KDE for bulk transmission — times the pre-HP load.
2. **Would another weather year's peaks change that?** Same pre-HP (or
   incremental) kWh 8760, same annual `$`/kW-yr, placed with that year's
   load-weighted top 100 — the usual PoP rule, `MW / sum(MW of those
   hours)`, not an equal `1/100`. Distribution ranks the CT zone. Bulk
   transmission ranks the New England system. The 2025 row is this
   allocation. It is **not** a second read of the filed file. The two 2025
   numbers differ because OCC-863 and the KDE spread the same annual
   dollars across many unequal hours, while PoP uses that year's top 100.
3. **How much extra MC does the heat pump cause?** After minus before.
   That is the small figure in the CT testimony.

Leave `batch` blank to skip the representative-home dollars and keep the
heatmaps of whatever MC years are on S3.

```{python}
#| label: mc-years

def mc_years_on_s3(kind: str) -> list[int]:
    prefix = (
        f"s3://data.sb/switchbox/marginal_costs/{STATE}/{kind}/"
        f"utility={profile['mc_utility']}/"
    )
    years = []
    for path in list_s3_subdirs(prefix):
        leaf = path.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if leaf.startswith("year="):
            years.append(int(leaf.split("=", 1)[1]))
    return sorted(years)


dist_years = mc_years_on_s3("dist_and_sub_tx")
bulk_years = mc_years_on_s3("bulk_tx")
```

```{python}
#| label: representative-load

COMPONENTS = (
    ("Distribution", "mc_dist_sub_tx"),
    ("Bulk transmission", "mc_bulk_tx"),
)


def shift_est(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """CAIRO billing kWh is naive UTC. Filed MC uses a fixed −5h clock.

    That is the alignment `building_delivery_mc_8760` uses. It is not civil
    daylight time: a July hour stays five hours behind UTC.
    """
    return df.with_columns(pl.col("timestamp").dt.offset_by("-5h"))


def shift_civil(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """UTC billing kWh onto America/New_York wall time, DST included.

    ISO `interval_start_et` is this clock. Use it when joining to historical
    system-load hours. Do not use it to join the filed MC file.
    """
    tz = getattr(df.schema["timestamp"], "time_zone", None)
    expr = pl.col("timestamp") if tz else pl.col("timestamp").dt.replace_time_zone("UTC")
    return df.with_columns(
        expr.dt.convert_time_zone("America/New_York").dt.replace_time_zone(None).alias("timestamp")
    )


def fossil_hourly_profiles() -> tuple[pl.DataFrame | None, pl.DataFrame | None]:
    batch = str(profile.get("batch") or "")
    if not batch:
        display(Markdown("No CAIRO `batch` in the profile, so the representative-home dollars are skipped."))
        return None, None
    utility = str(profile["electric_utility"])
    seg_before = segment_name(str(profile["scenario"]), "precalc")
    annual = cast(
        pl.DataFrame,
        load_master_bills(STATE, batch, seg_before)
        .filter(
            (pl.col("month") == "Annual")
            & (pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == utility)
            & (
                pl.col("heats_with_natgas")
                | pl.col("heats_with_oil")
                | pl.col("heats_with_propane")
            )
        )
        .select("bldg_id", "weight")
        .collect(),
    )
    ids = annual["bldg_id"].to_list()
    kwh_before = load_billing_kwh_8760(STATE, utility, batch, seg_before)
    before = weighted_avg_hourly(kwh_before, ids, annual)
    after: pl.DataFrame | None = None
    try:
        seg_after = segment_name(str(profile["scenario"]), "calibrated")
        kwh_after = load_billing_kwh_8760(STATE, utility, batch, seg_after)
        after = weighted_avg_hourly(kwh_after, ids, annual)
        after_note = " Post-retrofit uses the same buildings' upgrade-02 load."
    except Exception:
        after_note = " Post-retrofit load was not available, so the incremental charts are skipped."
    display(
        Markdown(
            f"The representative load is the weighted-average hourly kWh of "
            f"**{annual.height:,}** fossil homes "
            f"(survey weight {annual['weight'].sum():,.0f}) on {utility}."
            f"{after_note}"
        )
    )
    return before, after


load_before, load_after = fossil_hourly_profiles()
```

```{python}
#| label: household-mc-helpers

def civil_keys(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return shift_civil(df).with_columns(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.day().alias("day"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
    )


def seasonal_dollars(paid: pl.DataFrame) -> dict[str, float]:
    summer = float(paid.filter(pl.col("month").is_in(list(SUMMER_MONTHS)))["dollars"].sum())
    heating = float(paid.filter(pl.col("month").is_in(list(HEATING_MONTHS)))["dollars"].sum())
    return {"may_sep": summer, "oct_apr": heating, "annual": summer + heating}


def price_filed(load: pl.DataFrame, ref: pl.DataFrame, col: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    paid = (
        shift_est(load)
        .join(ref.select("timestamp", col), on="timestamp", how="inner")
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month"),
            (pl.col("kwh") * pl.col(col)).alias("dollars"),
        )
    )
    return seasonal_dollars(paid)


def topn_rate(year_load: pl.DataFrame, n: int, scalar: float) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Load-weighted PoP: top n hours, weight = MW / sum(MW), $/kWh = scalar × weight.

    A November fallback can put two timestamps on one wall-clock hour. Summing
    those weights keeps the annual $/kW-yr on the hour the home is billed for.
    """
    top = year_load.sort("load_mw", descending=True).head(n)
    total = float(top["load_mw"].sum())
    rates = top.with_columns((pl.col("load_mw") / total).alias("pop_weight")).select(
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.month().alias("month"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.day().alias("day"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour"),
        pl.col("pop_weight"),
        (pl.lit(scalar) * pl.col("pop_weight")).alias("mc_per_kwh"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.ordinal_day().alias("day_of_year"),
        pl.col("timestamp").dt.hour().alias("hour_of_day"),
    )
    return rates.group_by("month", "day", "hour").agg(
        pl.col("mc_per_kwh").sum(),
        pl.col("pop_weight").sum(),
        pl.col("day_of_year").first(),
        pl.col("hour_of_day").first(),
    )


def peak_series(component: str, year: int) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame | None, int]:
    """The load 8760 this component's PoP usually ranks, for one weather year."""
    use_bulk = component == "Bulk transmission" and (
        profile.get("bulk_zones") or profile.get("bulk_load_uri")
    )
    if use_bulk:
        if year not in bulk_by_year:
            try:
                frame = load_bulk_year(year)
            except Exception:
                frame = None
            if frame is not None and frame.height >= MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE:
                bulk_by_year[year] = frame
        return bulk_by_year.get(year), int(profile.get("bulk_n_peak_hours") or N_PEAK_HOURS)
    part = iso.filter(pl.col("year") == year)
    if part.height < MIN_HOURS_COMPLETE:
        return None, N_PEAK_HOURS
    return part, N_PEAK_HOURS


def price_topn(
    load: pl.DataFrame, year_load: pl.DataFrame, n: int, scalar: float
) -> dict[str, float]:
    rates = topn_rate(year_load, n, scalar)
    paid = (
        civil_keys(load)
        .join(
            rates.select("month", "day", "hour", "mc_per_kwh"),
            on=["month", "day", "hour"],
            how="left",
        )
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("mc_per_kwh").fill_null(0.0),
            (pl.col("kwh") * pl.col("mc_per_kwh")).alias("dollars"),
        )
    )
    return seasonal_dollars(paid)


def load_delta(before: pl.DataFrame, after: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return (
        before.rename({"kwh": "kwh_before"})
        .join(after.rename({"kwh": "kwh_after"}), on="timestamp")
        .with_columns((pl.col("kwh_after") - pl.col("kwh_before")).alias("kwh"))
        .select("timestamp", "kwh")
    )


def household_rows(
    load: pl.DataFrame, ref: pl.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame, pl.DataFrame]:
    filed_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    year_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for component, col in COMPONENTS:
        filed_rows.append({"component": component, **price_filed(load, ref, col)})
        scalar = float(ref[col].sum())
        for year in iso_complete_years:
            series, n_hours = peak_series(component, year)
            if series is None:
                continue
            year_rows.append(
                {
                    "year": str(year),
                    "component": component,
                    **price_topn(load, series, n_hours, scalar),
                }
            )
    return pl.DataFrame(filed_rows), pl.DataFrame(year_rows)


def show_household_gt(df: pl.DataFrame, title: str, subtitle: str) -> None:
    show_gt(
        df.with_columns(
            pl.col("may_sep").round(2),
            pl.col("oct_apr").round(2),
            pl.col("annual").round(2),
        ),
        title=title,
        subtitle=subtitle,
        labels={
            "component": "Component",
            "may_sep": "May–Sep ($/year)",
            "oct_apr": "Oct–Apr ($/year)",
            "annual": "Annual ($/year)",
        },
        num_cols=["may_sep", "oct_apr", "annual"],
        num_decimals=2,
    )


def show_year_gt(df: pl.DataFrame, title: str, subtitle: str) -> None:
    order = pl.Enum([name for name, _ in COMPONENTS])
    show_gt(
        df.with_columns(pl.col("component").cast(order))
        .sort("component", "year")
        .with_columns(pl.col("component").cast(pl.String))
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("year").cast(pl.Int64),
            pl.col("may_sep").round(2),
            pl.col("oct_apr").round(2),
            pl.col("annual").round(2),
        ),
        title=title,
        subtitle=subtitle,
        labels={
            "year": "Weather year",
            "component": "Component",
            "may_sep": "May–Sep ($/year)",
            "oct_apr": "Oct–Apr ($/year)",
            "annual": "Annual ($/year)",
        },
        num_cols=["may_sep", "oct_apr", "annual"],
        num_decimals=2,
    )


def plot_year_mc(year_df: pl.DataFrame, title: str) -> None:
    long = (
        year_df.select("year", "component", "may_sep", "oct_apr")
        .unpivot(index=["year", "component"], variable_name="season", value_name="dollars")
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("season").replace_strict({"may_sep": "May–Sep", "oct_apr": "Oct–Apr"}),
            pl.col("component").cast(pl.Enum([name for name, _ in COMPONENTS])),
        )
    )
    year_order = year_df["year"].unique(maintain_order=True).to_list()
    p = (
        ggplot(long, aes("year", "dollars", fill="season"))
        + geom_col()
        + scale_x_discrete(limits=year_order)
        + facet_wrap("component", ncol=1)
        + scale_fill_manual(
            values={"May–Sep": SB_COLORS["carrot"], "Oct–Apr": SB_COLORS["sky"]}
        )
        + labs(title=title, x="", y="$ / year", fill="")
        + theme_switchbox()
        + theme(figure_size=(10.5, 6.0))
    )
    display_figure(p.draw())
```

```{python}
#| label: pop-weight-helper

def plot_pop_weights(component: str, high: str) -> None:
    rows: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
    for year in iso_complete_years:
        series, n_hours = peak_series(component, year)
        if series is None:
            continue
        rows.append(
            topn_rate(series, n_hours, 1.0)
            .select("day_of_year", "hour_of_day", "pop_weight")
            .with_columns(pl.lit(str(year)).alias("year"))
        )
    if not rows:
        return
    heat = pl.concat(rows)
    p = (
        ggplot(heat, aes("day_of_year", "hour_of_day", fill="pop_weight"))
        + geom_tile()
        + facet_wrap("year", ncol=4)
        + scale_fill_gradient(low="#f8e3c4", high=high)
        + scale_x_continuous(
            breaks=[1, 91, 182, 274, 365],
            labels=["Jan", "Apr", "Jul", "Oct", "Dec"],
        )
        + scale_y_continuous(breaks=[0, 6, 12, 18, 23])
        + labs(title=component, x="", y="Hour", fill="Weight")
        + theme_switchbox()
        + theme(figure_size=(10.5, 4.2))
    )
    display_figure(p.draw())


```
